title: Predicting no-show appointments in a pediatric hospital in Chile using machine learning
summary: Machine-learning models used pediatric appointment records from a Chilean hospital (2015–2018) to predict no-shows with class-imbalance and cost-sensitive evaluation. The result is setting-specific retrospective prediction; no intervention effect was tested.
ai_technology: Cost-sensitive machine-learning classifiers predict pediatric hospital appointment no-shows.
organization: Center for Mathematical Modeling (CNRS IRL2807), University of Chile, Santiago, Chile.

evidence.tested: Full Springer PDF: pediatric no-show appointments in Chilean hospital were modeled with imbalanced-data and cost-aware metrics; retrospective 2015–2018 records support a setting-specific prediction/management result, not an intervention effect.
evidence.unknown: The model is retrospective and specific to one hospital; no intervention effect was evaluated.
evidence.ai_role: Cost-sensitive machine-learning classifiers predict pediatric hospital appointment no-shows.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
